lines.text: Vera, who actually picks the next word?
Nobody, yet. The network gives every token a score: a logit.
Then a separate, simple step chooses one: the sampler.
So the network scores, and the sampler picks.
But a score isn't a chance.
Softmax makes them probabilities that add up to one. “Practice” gets almost 32%.
lines.say: Softmax makes them probabilities that add up to one. Practice gets almost thirty-two percent.

lines.text: From a real model?
Hand-set words and scores. Real maths.
And the “creativity” setting in AI tools?
lines.say: And the creativity setting in A I tools?

lines.text: Temperature. The scores are divided by it before softmax.
Turn it down: the favourite takes over. At zero, always the top token.
Reliable!
Repeatable. Also dull, and prone to loops. Turn it up: the bars flatten.
So even “banana” gets a chance? Chaos.
lines.say: So even banana gets a chance? Chaos.

lines.text: How do you keep the nonsense out?
Cut the long tail. Top-k keeps a fixed number, say three.
lines.say: Cut the long tail. Top K keeps a fixed number, say three.

lines.text: Top-p keeps the smallest set adding up to 80%.
lines.say: Top P keeps the smallest set adding up to eighty percent.

lines.text: What's the difference?
Top-p adapts. Sure, like “Paris”: one word. Unsure: more.
lines.say: Top P adapts. Sure, like Paris: one word. Unsure: more.

lines.text: Say it picks “practice”. Then what?
lines.say: Say it picks practice. Then what?

lines.text: The pick joins the text, and the whole model runs again.
The whole model? Every time?
Every token. That's autoregressive generation.
So that's why answers appear word by word!
Vera, can I turn these dials myself?
Drag them in the Sampling chapter, or play The Dial in the game: you're the sampler.
Mission one: “make it boring”. Finally, something I'm good at.
lines.say: Mission one: make it boring. Finally, something I'm good at.
